title: Cross-team brief: rapid decisions and technical risk heatmap
summary: Compact notes from the cross-team engineering leadership check-in focused on fast unblock decisions for the upcoming canary rollout, a live technical risk heatmap, and a short update on incident backlog and SLO adjustments.
agenda: 15m - Canary rollout decision and fast-fallback policy
10m - Incident backlog triage and SLO tuning proposals
decisions: Approve phased canary for v2026.6.2 with initial 2% traffic on dedicated → hosted route, expand to 10% after 24h if no p50 regression >10%
Enable automated fallback to quantized model variant (q8_compat) for requests with latency > 90th percentile for 3 consecutive minutes
Hold SLO change for embeddings batch endpoints — not approved this week; more data requested
action_items: Marcus Chen to push routing policy change PR (runtime/router) and tag for emergency rollback, due 2026-06-11
Priya Nair to add a temporary alert that triggers on combined p50+p95 drift for the canary cohort, due 2026-06-10 EOD
Liam O'Connor to validate private deployment KMS key rotation window won't impact canary, report by 2026-06-12
Sofia Martinez to prepare a cost delta estimate for q8_compat fallback under 10% traffic (spreadsheet link in linked_artifacts), due 2026-06-11
Ava Ramirez to publish short runbook for on-call to execute model fallback and verification steps, due 2026-06-10
blockers: Unresolved query about KV cache warmup causing a transient latency spike in long-context requests (investigating with serving-runtime kernels team)
Capacity tagging mismatch between Dedicated autoscaler and billing metrics — delays on visibility for committed pools
Pending legal signoff on a new telemetry retention policy needed for customer A's private deployment audit
discussion_notes:
Start: meeting opened with a 3-minute check-in; each lead called out one immediate risk. Ava summarized the canary plan: v2026.6.2 contains two kernel changes and a new batching heuristic that reduce token exec time but may change p50 for short sequences. Marcus flagged a routing config that would need a quick rollback path; agreed to treat rollout as traffic-routed feature flag with explicit rollback PR.

Priya presented the heatmap (latency, cost, regression risk) and emphasized that while average latency looked fine in staging, p95 for some multi-turn chat traffic was noisy due to cold KV cache on longer sequences; proposed a short-term mitigation of prewarming the KV cache for canary cohort. The team debated cost of prewarm vs risk; decided to prewarm only for first 10% of canary requests and rely on fallback to q8_compat if latency remains high.

Incident backlog: Daniel walked through a prioritized list — two P2s related to tokenization edge-cases and one P1 from last week already mitigated but not closed. Team agreed to re-prioritize tokenization P2s to be fixed next sprint; engineering leads to allocate one engineer each from serving-runtime and platform-engineering.

SLO tuning: Eva proposed adjusting SLOs for some low-traffic endpoints to reduce pager noise; discussion concluded that we need 30 days of drift data before changes. Action: collect data and reconvene.

Risks & notes: legal telemetry signoff blocking a private-deployment customer was flagged as high business risk — Liam to escalate. Also noted that Dedicated autoscaler tagging mismatch is causing billing visibility gaps; Marcus to coordinate with finance and infra.

End: confirmed owners for each action item and agreed to a short async check-in 24 hours after canary starts. Next full cross-team leadership sync scheduled for 2026-06-17.
